    The coven

    Five scenes from the autumn wood. Tap one and the coven casts: a sigil draws itself in light, fractals outward and opens a doorway to somewhere else.

    Draw your own sigil

    Trace one stroke on the pad. It is mirrored six times, glows, and fractals into a portal. The closer to the centre you draw, the tighter the spell.

    Watchers in the branches

    Ravens are circling the whole page, eyes burning red. Click one as it passes. These two stayed still long enough to be photographed.

    A group of ravens is called an unkindness. A group of crows is a murder.
    Crows can learn to recognise individual human faces, and their neighbours pick up the grudge.
    Ravens can imitate sounds, including human speech, in captivity.
    Legend says the kingdom falls if the ravens leave the Tower of London. The Tower still keeps them.

    The apple oracle

    On Snap-Apple Night, people peeled an apple in one long strip and threw the peel over a shoulder to read the letter it made. Cut an apple across the middle and it holds a secret of its own.

    Tap an apple to cut it across the middle. Then touch the star inside.

    Wax works

    Real candles lose a little every minute. Light them and watch the wax pool and run. Bring your cursor near a flame and it leans away from you. Light all five for a séance.

    About the facts. Fact text is written from general knowledge of Halloween history, folklore and natural history. It has not been checked line by line against primary sources, so please verify anything you plan to repeat. Good places to start: Encyclopaedia Britannica and Smithsonian Magazine on Halloween history, Historic Royal Palaces on the Tower of London ravens, and the Barn Owl Trust on owls. The "ravens" in the photographs are dark birds that may be crows.
